title: Seminary Review Night
welcome: Join on your phone with the room code.
Answer on your phone, not out loud.
Points get bigger every round, and the finale lets you wager.

rounds.title: Quick Quiz
rounds.intro: Questions on what we've studied this year.
rules: A question and choices appear on the screen. Pick one on your phone.
The clock starts after the question is read aloud.
A correct answer scores. A faster correct answer scores a little more.

questions.q: Which scripture asks “Who shall stand in his holy place?”
questions.note: Psalm 24:3–4. “He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart.”

questions.q: Maya's friends want her to watch a movie with content she knows isn't right. Which scripture helps her most?
questions.note: Genesis 39:9. Joseph fled temptation and said sin is against God. Isaiah 5:20 and Joshua 24:15 also fit.

questions.q: Ethan made a serious mistake and wonders whether Jesus Christ can forgive him. Which scripture helps him most?
questions.note: Isaiah 1:18. “…they shall be as white as snow.”

questions.q: Ava is anxious about choosing classes and a future career. Which scripture helps her most?
questions.note: Proverbs 3:5–6. Trust in the Lord, and he shall direct thy paths.

questions.q: Caleb feels invisible at school and wonders whether his life has any purpose. Which scripture helps him most?
questions.note: Moses 1:39. God's work and glory is our immortality and eternal life. Abraham 3:22–23 and Genesis 1:26–27 also fit.

questions.q: Liam asks, “Why would anyone need a prophet today?” Which scripture helps most?
questions.note: Amos 3:7. The Lord reveals His secrets to His servants the prophets. Ezekiel 3:16–17 and Isaiah 29:13–14 also fit.

questions.q: Sam asks why Sunday should feel different from the other days of the week. Which scripture helps most?
questions.note: Isaiah 58:13–14. Call the sabbath a delight.

questions.q: Jordan's friend asks why he pays ten percent of his income to the Church. Which scripture helps most?
questions.note: Malachi 3:8–10. The Lord promises to open the windows of heaven.

questions.q: Riley feels like no one understands the pain they carry. Which scripture teaches that the Savior carried our griefs?
questions.note: Isaiah 53:3–5 “Surely [Jesus Christ] hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows.”

questions.q: Sophie wonders whether God knew her before she was born. Which scripture helps most?
Lucas wonders how the Lord warns His people of danger. Which scripture teaches that a prophet is like a watchman?
Zoe's friend says the Bible is enough and we don't need the Book of Mormon. Which scripture shows the two working together?

rounds.title: True or False
rules: A statement appears on the screen. Tap True or False on your phone.
The clock is short, so trust your first instinct.
A correct answer scores. A faster correct answer scores a little more.

statements.s: President Russell M. Nelson taught that in coming days it will not be possible to survive spiritually without the constant influence of the Holy Ghost.
statements.note: “Revelation for the Church, Revelation for Our Lives,” May 2018.

statements.s: Elder David P. Homer taught that the Spirit speaks to everyone in exactly the same way.
statements.note: He taught that the Spirit speaks to different people in different ways, and to the same person in different ways at different times (“Hearing His Voice,” May 2019).

statements.s: In 1 Kings 19, the Lord spoke to Elijah through a still, small voice rather than through the wind, the earthquake, or the fire.
Having questions or concerns about Heavenly Father, Jesus Christ, or Their gospel is normal.
statements.note: From the Acting in Faith lesson.

statements.s: President Jeffrey R. Holland counseled us to start a quest for faith by saying how much faith we do not have.
statements.note: He counseled the opposite: “be true to the faith you do have” (“Lord, I Believe,” May 2013).

statements.s: Elder Neil L. Andersen shared President Dallin H. Oaks's answer: “I don't know the answer to that question, but let me answer a question that I do know.”
Annotating scriptures includes marking, taking notes, and linking verses.
statements.note: The three skills practiced in the Annotating Scriptures lesson.

statements.s: Elder David A. Bednar taught that writing down what we learn as we study the scriptures is a powerful invitation to the Holy Ghost.
statements.note: “Because We Have Them before Our Eyes,” New Era, Apr. 2006.

statements.s: Preach My Gospel teaches that setting goals can help you make and keep covenants with God.
Elder Ulisses Soares taught that the Lord's help with our righteous goals is limited.
statements.note: He taught that it is unlimited, and that the Lord supports us in any good and righteous endeavor.

statements.s: Saying “At least it wasn't worse” is a good way to show empathy to someone who is sad.
statements.note: Statements that begin “At least …” do not communicate empathy.

statements.s: Saying “You don't have to talk if you don't want to, but I'm here to listen if you do” communicates empathy.
statements.note: From the Coping with Sadness lesson.

statements.s: President Russell M. Nelson taught that whatever questions or problems we have, the answer is always found in the life and teachings of Jesus Christ.
statements.note: “The Answer Is Always Jesus Christ,” May 2023.

statements.s: Feelings of sadness and discouragement mean a person lacks faith.
statements.note: Challenging emotions are a normal part of mortal life; Jesus Christ can help us carry them.

statements.s: The Lord fed Israel with manna in the wilderness.
Before he died, Joshua urged Israel to choose to serve the Lord.
Deborah and Gideon were among the deliverers the Lord raised up for Israel.
Naaman was healed of leprosy.
Micah taught us to do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God.
Ezekiel was called as a watchman for Israel during the Babylonian captivity.
The tabernacle and the ordinance of sacrifice taught about Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ.
In Moses 1, Moses learned that he was a child of God with a work to do.
Haggai taught the people to put God first.
Psalm 51 teaches that as we repent, the Savior can make us clean.
Isaiah 49 teaches that the Lord will not forget us.
Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of preparing Egypt for a war.
statements.note: He prepared Egypt for a famine (Genesis 41). Genesis 41

statements.s: Job lost his trust in the Lord because of his trials.
statements.note: Job kept trusting the Lord. Job 1

statements.s: The Fall was an accident that was never part of Heavenly Father's plan.
statements.note: The Fall was a necessary step in the plan, and Jesus Christ redeems us from its effects. Moses 4

statements.s: In the premortal life, Satan sought to protect our agency.
statements.note: Satan sought to destroy our agency. Moses 4

statements.s: Ecclesiastes teaches that the things of this world last forever.
statements.note: Ecclesiastes teaches that the things of this world are temporary. Ecclesiastes 1

statements.s: Jeremiah prophesied the gathering of Israel in the latter days.
Beginning in Isaiah 40, Isaiah wrote to comfort Jews who would later be captive in Babylon.
Isaiah 54 teaches that the Lord's anger with Israel would last forever.
statements.note: Isaiah 54:9 compares it to the flood: it ended, and the Lord's anger would not be forever. Isaiah 54:9

statements.s: In Isaiah 54:10, the Lord says His kindness will last longer than the mountains and hills.
In Jeremiah 18, once the clay is marred, the potter throws it away.
statements.note: The potter reworks the clay into a new vessel: the Lord patiently helps us change (Jeremiah 18:1–6). Jeremiah 18:1–6

statements.s: Isaiah 9:2 describes Jesus Christ as a great light for people who walk in darkness.
Job's story teaches the hope that comes through the Resurrection.
Isaiah 44–47 teaches us to put Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ before anyone or anything else.
Isaiah 61 teaches that the Savior can only heal physical sickness.
statements.note: Isaiah 61 teaches that the Savior can heal, free, and comfort us in every way. Isaiah 61

statements.s: Jeremiah 36 shows how the scriptures can turn us to Jesus Christ for forgiveness.

rounds.title: Put It in Order
rounds.intro: Put events, verses, or steps in the right order.
rules: Your phone shows a mixed-up list.
Tap the items in order, first to last, then lock in.
You score for every item in the right place, plus a bonus for a perfect order.

Gomer accrues debt and gives all of her gifts from Hosea to Baal

rounds.title: Fake Out
rounds.intro: Write a believable fake ending, then find the real one.
rules: Your set of 3 or 4 gets one clue. Write a fake ending that sounds real.
Everyone else sees the real ending mixed in with the fakes and picks the one they trust.
Pick the real one and score. Fool a classmate with your fake and score every time.

rounds.title: Sketch It

rules: Your set draws the same story on your phone. No words or letters.
Everyone else sees the drawings and guesses which story it is.
Guess right and score. Draw clearly, because you score when classmates guess your story. Pick a favorite drawing for a bonus.

rounds.title: Apply It
rounds.intro: Use a scripture to answer a real-life situation.
rules: Your set of 3 or 4 gets the same situation and scripture.
Each of you writes how the scripture helps, in a sentence or two.
Everyone else votes for the answer they like best. You score for every vote, and the top answer gets a bonus.
